title: Hong Kong Officials Raid Home of Media Mogul Critical of Beijing

image.attribution: 海彥, Voice of America / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Hong Kong anti-corruption officials have raided the home of media mogul Jimmy Lai, whose publications are often critical of mainland China.

The early Thursday raid comes after local media this month published reports claiming Lai made major donations to pro-democracy lawmakers. Lai denies any wrongdoing. There are no laws in Hong Kong that require the disclosure of political donations.

Officials also raided the home of pro-democracy lawmaker Lee Cheuk-yan, whose Labor Party played a major part in the recent Occupy Central protests against Chinese influence in Hong Kong.

Many in the semi-autonomous Chinese region are concerned at what they see as the erosion of press freedom, as well as the Communist Party’s insistence that it vet candidates for Hong Kong’s 2017 election.

Occupy Central protesters have held a series of major demonstrations and are threatening to take over the financial district if Beijing does not promise to allow a fully democratic election.

Lai owns a wide range of publications that have often been supportive of the protests. Following the raid, shares in Lai’s Next Media Ltd fell as much as six percent before trading was halted.

questions.question: Why did Hong Kong anti-corruption officials raid Jimmy Lai’s home?
options: To investigate allegations that he made major donations to pro-democracy lawmakers
To arrest him for violating election laws
To question him about foreign government funding
To respond to complaints about his newspapers
questions.answer: To investigate allegations that he made major donations to pro-democracy lawmakers

questions.question: Was Jimmy Lai the only person whose home was raided?
options: Yes, only Jimmy Lai’s home was raided
No, officials also raided the home of pro-democracy lawmaker Lee Cheuk-yan
Yes, but only after his newspapers were criticized
No, but the authorities raided no other political figures
questions.answer: No, officials also raided the home of pro-democracy lawmaker Lee Cheuk-yan

questions.question: What are the Occupy Central protesters threatening to do if Beijing does not promise a fully democratic election?
options: Hold a general strike across all of Hong Kong
Demand immediate independence from mainland China
